candidates.title: Entity-class identity degrades to a stringly-typed &str at the build_class_sampler seam, where a correctness rule is gated by string equality

evidence.reading: `ClassSchemes` already carries the class identity as three typed fields (`inflow`/`load`/`ncs`, confirmed in context.rs:17-23), and `ClassDimensions` mirrors it. But `build_forward_sampler` flattens that typed identity back to bare string literals `"inflow"`/`"load"`/`"ncs"` passed via `ClassSamplerParams.class_name: &str`, and `build_class_sampler` then gates a real correctness rule — Historical replay is inflow-only — on `class_name != "inflow"` string comparison (not merely diagnostics; the diagnostic `format!("historical_{class_name}")` is a separate, legitimate use). A class rename or a typo in one of the three literals compiles cleanly and silently mis-gates. The class set is closed and small (inflow/load/ncs are entity classes, not paradigm nouns), so a typed class discriminant would be L1-pure with three consumers, not one.

candidates.fixShape: Introduce a small closed class discriminant (e.g. an entity-class enum with `Inflow|Load|Ncs`) carried on `ClassSamplerParams` in place of the `&str`, so the Historical-only-for-inflow gate becomes a match/`==` on a typed value the compiler checks, and the three build sites pass the variant instead of a literal. Keep the human-readable label for diagnostics as a `Display`/`as_str` off that enum so error messages are unchanged. Purely local type-safety; advances no roadmap phase and introduces no engine vocabulary.

candidates.title: ForwardSamplerConfig is both a store handle and a parameter bag, and is the point where the generation-side and realized-value halves straddle

evidence.command: git show a136840d4f2ea137f685f0af6dac04254b983b60:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/sampling/mod.rs | sed -n '262,289p'; echo ---; git show a136840d4f2ea137f685f0af6dac04254b983b60:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/sampling/mod.rs | sed -n '421,434p'
evidence.reading: The single #[derive(Copy)] seam type carries, in one flat bundle, a persistent store handle (`ctx: &StochasticContext`, whose own doc says it provides `tree, seeds, correlation, and entity order` — all generation-side artifacts: the fitted-PAR opening tree, the base/forward seeds, the pre-decomposed correlation) alongside four realized-value `Option<&…Library>` references plus per-run `class_schemes`/`stages`/`dims`. `build_forward_sampler` (line 403) unpacks the config and reads ONLY generation-side accessors off `ctx` (`forward_seed()`, `base_seed()`, `entity_order()`, `tree_view()`, `correlation()`), while the library options are the realized-value inputs. So the answer to seam-shape Q3 is `both` — a store handle AND a parameter bag — and this is also the Q2 straddle: `ForwardSamplerConfig` is the one public sampling type that spans the generation-only / realized-value boundary. The validity coupling (which of the four libraries must be `Some`) is not encoded in the type; it is discovered at runtime in `build_class_sampler` against `class_schemes`.

candidates.fixShape: Split the one flat bundle into two clearly-named halves at the seam: a persistent store handle (today `&StochasticContext`; the generation-side tree/seeds/correlation/entity-order the sampler consumes read-only) and a transient per-run realized-value source selection (the four library references plus the per-class schemes that pick and require them). The source-selection half is where the four-way validity coupling lives and should own a constructor/validation that makes the `scheme -> required library` pairing a type-level fact rather than a runtime check in `build_class_sampler`; leave the coupling-collapse mechanics themselves to the over-engineering sibling lens. This keeps the store as a store and the source-selection as a bag, so a reader of the seam sees two concerns, not eight peer fields. Roadmap note only (not executed here): under Part IV/V the realized-value libraries and the generation tree both fold into a single `Switchable<T>` uncertainty store, at which point the store half and most of the source bag collapse into one owner — the split proposed now is the shape that survives that move. Must stay L1-pure: no engine/paradigm noun enters the type, no dependency on an engine crate, and the source-selection type has multiple consumers (every cobre-sddp `ForwardSamplerConfig` construction site), so it is not a one-consumer abstraction.

candidates.title: standardize_external_inflow's #[allow(too_many_arguments)] rationale ('no natural sub-grouping exists') is contradicted by the derived-seed 4-tuple being re-threaded verbatim through four signatures across two crates

evidence.output: // Rationale: the accumulator seed pair joins the lag-values seed pair; no // natural sub-grouping exists that would not just relocate the arity into a // literal struct. #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] pub fn standardize_external_inflow(library, external_rows, hydro_ids, stages, par, derived_lag_values: &[f64], l_state: usize, derived_accum: &[f64], derived_weight: &[f64], stage_lag_transitions, downstream_par_order: usize)
evidence.reading: The rationale asserts the four seed inputs (derived_lag_values, l_state, derived_accum, derived_weight) have 'no natural sub-grouping'. The code contradicts that: the same 4-tuple is re-declared verbatim as positional parameters in run_eta_inversion (eta_inversion.rs:37, passed straight through) and in standardize_historical_windows (historical.rs:296, whose own comment at line 292 says it 'mirrors standardize_external_inflow's inputs'), and in the caller build_external_inflow_library (cobre-sddp setup/scenario_libraries.rs:110, whose comment at line 103 again claims 'a context struct would just relocate the arity, not reduce it'). run_eta_inversion resets lag_state (from derived_lag_values), lag_accum (from derived_accum) and lag_weight_accum (from derived_weight) TOGETHER at every outer-loop boundary, i.e. they are operationally one seed. A 4-tuple re-declared across four signatures in two crates is a natural aggregate by construction. 'Would just relocate the arity' is false: the struct is built ONCE where the seed is computed and passed by reference to all four consumers, so arity is reduced at four sites, not relocated; and because derived_lag_values / derived_accum / derived_weight are all &[f64] of equal length, the positional form admits a silent transposition at each of the four call sites that a named struct eliminates.

candidates.fixShape: Introduce a by-reference aggregate for the stage-0 derived seed, e.g. DerivedSeed<'a> { lag_values: &'a [f64], l_state: usize, accum: &'a [f64], weight: &'a [f64] }, constructed once where the seed is computed and passed as a single argument through standardize_external_inflow, run_eta_inversion, standardize_historical_windows, and the caller build_external_inflow_library. The shared per-hydro canonical-position ordering and 'empty accum means reset-to-zero' invariant, currently restated in three near-identical doc-comment blocks, attaches to the type once. This shrinks the 11-arg / 14-arg / 12-arg signatures and removes the same-typed &[f64] transposition hazard. This does NOT dispute the mirror's blanket sanction of allow-with-rationale as a load-bearing lint class; it disputes only the factual claim of this specific rationale. Once the seed is a struct the #[allow(too_many_arguments)] can be dropped from these functions. Multiple consumers (four), so not a one-consumer abstraction; no engine or paradigm noun, so no L1-purity conflict. Blast radius: three functions in this crate plus build_external_inflow_library in cobre-sddp (cited, not anchored).

candidates.title: ForwardSamplerConfig encodes a per-class scheme x library validity matrix as four independent Option<&Library> fields, so invalid scheme/library pairings are representable and caught only at runtime

evidence.output: pub struct ForwardSamplerConfig<'a> { class_schemes: ClassSchemes, ctx, stages, dims, historical_library: Option<&'a HistoricalScenarioLibrary> (Required when class_schemes.inflow == Some(Historical)), external_inflow_library: Option<&'a ExternalScenarioLibrary> (Required when inflow == Some(External)), external_load_library (Required when load == Some(External)), external_ncs_library (Required when ncs == Some(External)) } ... build_class_sampler: Historical => historical_library.ok_or_else(|| MissingScenarioSource{reason: historical replay scheme selected but no historical library was loaded}); External => external_library.ok_or_else(|| MissingScenarioSource{reason: external scenario scheme selected but no external library was loaded})
evidence.reading: The four Options are not four independent knobs. build_forward_sampler pairs class_schemes.inflow with EITHER historical_library OR external_inflow_library (mutually exclusive by inflow scheme), and hard-wires historical_library: None for the load and ncs classes so they read only external_load_library / external_ncs_library. Validity is a (3 class x scheme) matrix flattened into 4 loosely-typed Options: each field is required-iff a corresponding class_schemes.<class> value, and the requirement is enforced only at runtime via StochasticError::MissingScenarioSource. The type therefore admits inflow==Some(External) with external_inflow_library==None (a runtime error) and inflow==InSample with a library Some (silently ignored dead input). The doc comments themselves restate the four-way coupling ('Required when class_schemes.inflow == Some(Historical)' etc.), which is the coupling that the type does not encode.

candidates.fixShape: Fold each class's scheme selector and its required library into one per-class source enum whose data-bearing variants carry the borrow: e.g. InflowSource { InSample, OutOfSample, Historical(&HistoricalScenarioLibrary), External(&ExternalScenarioLibrary) } and a LoadSource / NcsSource with only { InSample, OutOfSample, External(&ExternalScenarioLibrary) } (load and ncs never take a historical library, so the hard-wired historical_library: None disappears). build_forward_sampler then matches per-class variants instead of pairing a scheme with a maybe-present Option, so the scheme-to-library requirement becomes a compile-time consequence, the InSample-with-library silent-ignore state stops being representable, and the two mutually-exclusive inflow libraries can no longer both be Some. The MissingScenarioSource diagnostics move up to the config-construction boundary (where a library is or is not built), preserving the 'provide the external scenario file' / 'set a seed in stages.json' guidance. Not a one-consumer abstraction (three consumers: inflow, load, ncs); introduces no engine or paradigm noun, so no L1-purity conflict. Blast radius: ForwardSamplerConfig, build_forward_sampler, build_class_sampler, ClassSamplerParams in this crate, plus the ForwardSamplerConfig construction sites in cobre-sddp (simulation/state.rs, training/forward/sampler.rs, training/forward_pass_state.rs) cited as ripple, not anchored here.

candidates.title: OutOfSample QmcSobol forward draws re-derive the Sobol direction matrix + scramble params per scenario; the dormant `SobolPrecomputed` hoist is never wired (its `Some` branch is dead in production)

On the OutOfSample QmcSobol path each such call reaches fill_uncorrelated with sobol_ctx == None, so scrambled_sobol_point rebuilds the direction matrix (dim x [u32;32]) and the scramble-params vector every draw. Direction matrix and scramble params depend only on (forward_seed, iteration, noise_group_id, dim) — invariant across the entire scenario axis at a fixed stage. SobolPrecomputed (qmc_sobol/mod.rs:169) exists precisely to build these once per (seed,iteration,stage,dim) and reuse across scenarios, and fill_uncorrelated already carries the `sobol_ctx: Option<&SobolPrecomputed>` seam (line 84) — but the sole production caller hard-codes None, leaving the hoist unused and its Some branch dead.

candidates.mechanism: Per (iteration, scenario, stage) forward draw, scrambled_sobol_point heap-allocates a Vec<[u32;32]> of `dim` direction vectors (running the Joe-Kuo polynomial recurrence, O(dim*32*degree)) plus a Vec<(u32,u32)> of scramble params (seeding an RNG and drawing 2*dim u32). Both are constant across the scenario axis at a fixed (iteration, stage), so the work is redone n_scenarios times per stage per iteration instead of once. The SobolPrecomputed hoist and the `sobol_ctx` seam already exist to amortize it but are never wired from the forward sampler.
candidates.fixShape: Give the OutOfSample class sampler (or the caller that owns the per-(iteration,stage) loop) a per-stage SobolPrecomputed cache keyed on (forward_seed, iteration, noise_group_id, dim), built once when the stage/iteration first appears and reused across every scenario draw, then pass Some(&ctx) into the already-present `sobol_ctx` parameter of fill_uncorrelated so the precomputed branch (currently dead) is taken. No change to the generator body is needed (SobolPrecomputed / scrambled_sobol_point_precomputed already exist in the tree-noise crate). Determinism is preserved bit-for-bit because SobolPrecomputed::new derives its seed from the same derive_opening_seed(sampling_seed, iteration, stage_id) the point function uses, and the per-scenario XOR/scramble math is identical. The cache lifetime/ownership decision is a sampler-side concern in this sub-station; the tree-noise crate ships the primitive unchanged.

candidates.title: OutOfSample LHS forward draws regenerate a full Fisher-Yates permutation of `total_scenarios` per dimension per scenario, giving O(dim * total_scenarios^2) work per stage across the scenario axis

evidence.command: git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/sampling/out_of_sample.rs | sed -n '92,102p' ; git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/tree/lhs.rs | sed -n '/pub fn sample_lhs_point/,/^}/p'
evidence.output: out_of_sample.rs Lhs arm: `sample_lhs_point(&lhs_spec, output, perm_scratch);` (line 101). sample_lhs_point (tree/lhs.rs): `let perm = &mut perm_scratch[..n];` (n = total_scenarios) then `for slot in output.iter_mut().take(spec.dim) { for (i,p) in perm.iter_mut().enumerate() { *p = i; } fisher_yates(perm, &mut perm_rng); let stratum = perm[scenario_idx]; ... }`. The full 0..n permutation is re-initialized and fully shuffled once per output slot (per entity/dimension), and only perm[scenario_idx] is read from each.
evidence.reading: For a single (iteration, scenario, stage) point of `dim` entities, sample_lhs_point performs `dim` complete Fisher-Yates shuffles over `n = total_scenarios` elements — O(dim * total_scenarios) per point — but extracts only one stratum index per dimension. Called once per scenario across the whole forward set, the per-stage cost is O(dim * total_scenarios^2). The permutation for a given dimension is identical for every scenario at a fixed (iteration, stage) (perm_rng is reseeded from derive_opening_seed(sampling_seed, iteration, stage_id), independent of scenario) — the in-code comment 'perm_rng advances identically on all workers, so the permutation matches' confirms it is scenario-invariant — so the entire shuffle is recomputed n_scenarios times to read n_scenarios different indices out of the same permutation.

candidates.mechanism: The point-wise LHS generator recomputes, for every scenario, the same per-dimension stratification permutation of all `total_scenarios` strata (a full Fisher-Yates each), reading a single index. Because the permutation is scenario-invariant at a fixed (iteration, stage), the forward pass pays O(dim * total_scenarios^2) per stage where O(dim * total_scenarios) suffices — a quadratic-in-scenario recompute (not an allocation, perm_scratch is caller-owned; the cost is redundant shuffling) on the forward hot path.
candidates.fixShape: Hoist the per-(iteration,stage) LHS permutation set across the scenario axis: build the `dim` stratification permutations once per (forward_seed, iteration, noise_group_id, total_scenarios) into a per-stage cache (a stride-dim*n usize buffer, or a batch already produced by the tree-noise `generate_lhs` batch path), then each scenario reads its stratum column with no reshuffle. The draw RNG stays per-(scenario,dimension) so stratified values remain distinct. Owning the permutation cache is a sampler-side concern in this sub-station; the batch permutation primitive lives in tree-noise (cross-reference the existing generate_lhs batch generator). Determinism preserved: perm_rng seeding is unchanged, so the same permutation and the same stratum-per-scenario are produced bit-for-bit.

candidates.title: OutOfSample QmcHalton forward draws rebuild the prime sieve and a `total_scenarios`-sized Vec<Vec<Vec<u32>>> scramble table on every scenario; no precompute hoist exists

evidence.command: git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/sampling/out_of_sample.rs | sed -n '125,135p' ; git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/tree/qmc_halton/mod.rs | sed -n '261,290p' ; git show a136840d:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/tree/qmc_halton/mod.rs | grep -nE 'fn build_scramble_tables|Vec<Vec<Vec<u32>>>|fn sieve_primes'
evidence.output: out_of_sample.rs QmcHalton arm: `scrambled_halton_point(&halton_spec, output);` (line 134). scrambled_halton_point (qmc_halton/mod.rs:261) per call: `let primes = sieve_primes(spec.dim); let tables = build_scramble_tables(seed, &primes, spec.total_scenarios as usize);` then a per-dim loop. build_scramble_tables (qmc_halton/mod.rs:119) returns `Vec<Vec<Vec<u32>>>` (`let mut tables = Vec::with_capacity(primes.len())`, per-dim `Vec<Vec<u32>>` of max_digits entries, each a `Vec<u32>` permutation of the prime base). sieve_primes allocates `vec![false; upper_bound+1]` then collects.
evidence.reading: Same per-(iteration,scenario,stage) call site as candidate 1 (fill_uncorrelated with sobol_ctx None; the Halton arm has no ctx parameter at all). Every forward draw re-runs a prime sieve and rebuilds a three-level nested Vec of scramble permutation tables whose outer extent scales with dim and whose inner permutations are sized by the prime bases; the digit depth is derived from spec.total_scenarios. These tables depend only on (forward_seed, iteration, noise_group_id, dim, total_scenarios) and are identical for every scenario at a stage, yet are freshly heap-allocated and recomputed for each scenario draw. Unlike Sobol there is no HaltonPrecomputed type, so even the seam is absent.

candidates.mechanism: Per forward draw, scrambled_halton_point allocates a fresh prime sieve (Vec<bool> of upper_bound) and a nested Vec<Vec<Vec<u32>>> of Owen/Faure-style scramble permutation tables (outer length dim, middle length ~digit-depth(total_scenarios), inner length prime-base), then reads a single point out of it. All of this is invariant across the scenario axis, so at a stage with n_scenarios forward passes the sieve and the nested-Vec table are built n_scenarios times instead of once — a per-scenario allocation storm plus redundant table construction on the forward hot path.
candidates.fixShape: Mirror the Sobol hoist: introduce a per-(iteration,stage) precomputed Halton context (a HaltonPrecomputed holding the prime list and the scramble tables) built once per (forward_seed, iteration, noise_group_id, dim, total_scenarios) and reused across every scenario draw.
